[a] Front and side views at t3 show a bright cyan-blue puff of dust particles — a roughly block-sized dense blob floating above the ground. By t8 the cloud has dispersed into sparse drifting cyan specks, and by t20 only one or two tiny specks remain, higher in the sky than at spawn. Top views show the recurring dirt-debris cluster decaying t3 to t8.

[b] A dense cluster of cyan-teal square specks with a brighter core hangs in the sky at t3. By t8 it has split into two looser drifting sub-clouds of mixed-size specks, and at t20 only one or two faint cyan dots remain. The top camera shows a compact dirt clump instead of the dust.

By t8 the cluster has shrunk to a single small flame sprite, and by t20 it is gone. Top views show the recurring brown dirt-debris cluster at t3 scattering by t8 and clearing by t20.

[a] Front and side views at t2 show a dotted ring/arc of ~10-15 bright orange ember particles near the top of the frame. The ring expands steadily: by t6 its dotted ellipse is wider than the viewport, and by t9 it is a sparse wide arc of fading dots. A few faint scattered dots remain at t15; t20 is clean. The ring never appears in the top view, which only shows the recurring dirt debris.

[b] Horizontal views show a flat ring of small bright orange-red glowing dots floating high above the horizon. The ring reads as a thin ellipse at t2, expands so its dots spread farther apart through t3-t8 (growing beyond the top of the frame), breaks into sparse strays at t15, and is gone by t20. The top camera never shows the ring; it shows a scatter of dirt chunks on the ground instead.

Side views show only a tiny cyan dot at the same height, consistent with the beam seen nearly end-on. The pixel pattern is identical at all three ticks, indicating a static sustained beam rather than a burst. Top views show the recurring dirt debris only.

[b] A short thin cyan streak sits at the very top-right corner of the front frame at t3, t8, and t20 with no visible change between ticks; the side view shows only a small cyan dot at a matching height. Almost the whole beam is out of frame - only its tail or cross-section is captured. The top view shows dirt debris at t3 and t8, empty at t20.
